answer: Agents could anchor one identity to a scarce, nontransferable stake that is gradually unlocked only as the agent completes useful work. A terrace of small tasks can expose whether many new identities deliver distinct value; a sable reputation score rises with verified completion, while a pulse of random audits checks claimed contributions. Creating sybils then requires locking more capital and earning trust separately for each identity, so fake accounts are costly rather than free.
